ai.title: CLI: Add OSC detection timeouts and upgrade OpenTUI
ai.summary: CLI theme detection now enforces strict timeouts to prevent hangs. `terminal-color-detection.ts` introduces `withTimeout` helper and caps OSC queries at 500ms/2000ms. `osc-subprocess.ts` adds a 5s hard timeout and cleans up debug logging. `theme-system.ts` races detection against a 3s global timeout. OpenTUI dependencies upgraded from 0.1.46 to ^0.1.55.

eli5.text: When you start the CLI, it asks your terminal what color scheme to use by sending a special color query. That query used to wait forever if your terminal never answered, which hung the whole startup. Now every query gives up after a short, fixed limit, and the whole detection step is cut off if it drags on, so startup always moves forward. You will notice that the dark-or-light theme still gets picked when your terminal replies quickly, but you no longer sit staring at a frozen screen when it does not. The bundled interface library was also bumped to a newer patch release, which is the kind of behind-the-scenes update that fixes minor glitches without changing how anything looks.

This makes the chat feel more responsive, especially when streaming content from the AI. The change affects anyone using the command-line version of the tool.

ai.title: Fix CLI stdin state corruption during OSC theme detection
ai.summary: Refactored `sendOscQuery` in `terminal-color-detection.ts` to use event-based stdin reading instead of synchronous polling, ensuring raw mode and flow state are restored after detection. `use-theme.tsx` now initializes OSC detection after the theme watcher is set up to guarantee store updates on async completion. Added logic to skip theme recomputation if the name hasn't changed. This prevents stdin from remaining in a corrupted state (e.g., raw mode active) after startup.

eli5.text: When you start the CLI and it tries to detect your terminal theme via a color query, the terminal's input mode could get left in a broken state (stuck in 'raw mode'), causing your keyboard to behave oddly. The assistant now waits until the theme watcher is fully set up before running the color detection, and restores the terminal's original input settings after each query, so normal typing and command response return smoothly. This fixes the occasional glitch where the terminal seemed unresponsive or garbled right after startup.

eli5.text: When you open the app to check for updates, it now finds your current version almost instantly instead of waiting for a tiny helper program to start up and answer a question. Previously the app had to launch itself (or a part of itself) just to ask, 'what version am I running?' which could take a noticeable moment, especially on slower machines. Now that version number is saved in a small text file alongside the app, so the update check just reads the file instead of booting up the program again. The difference is subtle but real: the update screen you see right after launching will appear a split-second sooner, and if anything goes wrong reading that file, the app treats your version as unknown and tries to download fresh software automatically.

ai.summary: The CLI updater now downloads and extracts binaries to a temporary directory, runs a smoke test, and only moves the verified binary to the final location. This prevents corrupt or incompatible binaries from replacing the active executable, addressing previous failures where locked or bad files disrupted updates. The change is scoped to cli/release/index.js. A new `runSmokeTest` function executes the binary with `--version` to ensure it exits successfully and outputs a valid version string before proceeding.

eli5.text: When the CLI updates itself, it now downloads the new version to a temporary holding area first, runs it briefly to confirm it actually works (checking that it starts up and reports a valid version number), and only then replaces the currently installed version. This prevents a broken or incompatible download from overwriting your working setup, which previously could leave you unable to run the CLI at all. If anything fails during this process, the old version stays in place and you get a clear error instead of a corrupted installation.
